brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Hex bases on level 0 (full centre piece, full at (-1,0), (0,1), half-n at (-1,1), half-s at (0,-1), half-w at (1,0)) with level 1 bases at (0,0), (-1,0), (0,1). Two storeys, 12 parts incl. snaps; check_build meshClash clear.
Two drawers on level 0: drawer:0#-1,1#cut (style s) on the half-n base and drawer:0#0,-1#cut (style n) on the half-s base.
Footprint is about 382 x 160 x 497 mm. Sized to sit on a bench, but no bench-specific mounting (feet or bolt-down) was added, and the top-level bases are not fixed to a bench.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey hex storage tower with two drawers on the lower level. Joints are locked and the mesh check is clear. Capping every open face was refused because the cap would clash with the drawer frame, so several outer faces remain open (informational only). No props were added since the brief is about storage structure.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
